bookTitle: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis

facts.statement: Every candlestick consists of seven fundamental structural elements: open, high, low, close, upper wick, lower wick, and spread (the price distance between open and close), with wicks and spread being most revealing when validated by volume.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: In any candle, there are seven key elements. The open, high, low and close, the upper and lower wicks and the spread as shown in Fig 3.10... it is the wicks and the spread which are the most revealing.

facts.statement: The spread measures net session sentiment: a wide spread indicates strong bullish or bearish conviction, while a narrow spread indicates weak sentiment and lack of commitment among market participants.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: A wide spread between the open and the close indicates strong market sentiment... A narrow spread between the open and the close indicates sentiment which is weak.

facts.statement: Across any timeframe from tick charts to monthly charts, intrasession price action oscillates like a sine wave as buyers and sellers battle for supremacy, culminating in the completed candle structure.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Perhaps the simplest way to visualise the price action contained within a candle... is to display the price action, as a sine wave, with the market oscillating back and forth, as buyers and sellers battle for supremacy.

facts.topic: First Point of Focus: Wick Analysis
facts.statement: The length and context of any wick is always the primary point of focus in VPA because it instantly reveals impending strength, weakness, indecision, and changes in market sentiment.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: The length of any wick, either to the top or bottom of the candle is ALWAYS the first point of focus because it instantly reveals, impending strength, weakness, and indecision.

facts.statement: A deep lower wick forms when sellers dominate early but buyers absorb all selling pressure at lower levels, driving the price back up; this signals complete sentiment reversal and underlying buying strength.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Here we have a wick where the price has opened, the market has moved lower, and then recovered to close back at the open price... selling pressure in the first part of the session was completely absorbed.

facts.statement: An upper wick forms when buyers push prices higher at the open but encounter heavy resistance, allowing sellers to take control and push prices back down; this signals bearish rejection and exhaustion of buying momentum.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: We have a wick where the price has opened, the market has moved higher and then moved lower to close back at the open... early bullish sentiment turns into bearish dominance.

facts.statement: A candle featuring a deep lower or upper wick paired with a zero spread (where close equals open) carries just as much analytical significance as a wide-spread trend candle.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: A candle with a deep lower wick and zero spread (close equals open) is just as significant as a wide-spread candle.

facts.statement: A Hammer features a deep lower wick and narrow body signaling market strength and insider buying, while a Shooting Star features a deep upper wick and narrow body signaling market weakness and forced selling.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Shooting Star: Characterised by a deep upper wick and narrow body... Hammer: Characterised by a deep lower wick and narrow body, signalling potential market strength.

facts.statement: VPA examines linear volume-price relationships over time using horizontal bars along the X-axis, whereas Volume at Price (VAP) maps volume distribution across price levels using a vertical histogram along the Y-axis.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Primary Focus: Linear relationship between volume and price over time... Volume distribution across price levels... Horizontal volume bars along the bottom... Vertical volume histogram along the side.

facts.topic: Complementary Triangulation of VPA and VAP
facts.statement: Volume at Price (VAP) does not replace VPA but enhances it by providing an internal view of volume density across price levels, making invisible support and resistance barriers visually apparent.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: VAP does not replace traditional VPA; it enhances it. VPA monitors linear momentum over time, while VAP maps price congestion levels to confirm platforms of support or ceilings of resistance.

facts.statement: Analyzing a 5-day Microsoft 15-minute chart, VAP revealed massive volume concentration at bottom congestion defining a support platform, while extreme VAP volume at the top without price progress exposed heavy insider selling preceding a $1.40 drop.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Coulling highlights a 15-minute MSFT chart over a 5-day period... extreme VAP volume bar over just one day... revealed heavy insider selling... MSFT stock fell $1.40 like a stone.

generalAssumptions: Market price manipulation is structurally transparent on the volume tape.
Effort versus result governs institutional capital movement.
